message.content: {"caption":"Two-panel chart comparing early learning curves with stacked performance bars across training settings.","description":"The left line chart, “Short-term Performance (0–20 steps),” plots Avg@4 (%) against Training Steps at 0, 10, and 20. Its five series are a gray dashed Baseline, orange Navi(ê̂_high = 0.4), blue Navi(ê̂_high = 0.6), green Navi(ê̂_high = 0.8), and purple Navi(ê̂_high = 1.0). All rise over the plotted steps. The purple series is highest at 10 and 20 steps; at 20 steps the printed endpoint labels are 45.2 (purple), 44.0 (green), 43.0 (Baseline), 40.8 (blue), and 39.5 (orange). The right chart, “Long-term Performance (20–80 steps),” compares Baseline and Navi (0.4), Navi (0.6), Navi (0.8), and Navi (1.0), with Avg@4 (%) on a vertical axis that begins at 30. Each bar is stacked: the solid lower portion is Step 0–20 and the diagonally hatched upper portion is Step 20–80. Approximate readings at the top of the solid portions are 43, 39.5, 40.5, 44, and 45, respectively; the approximate cumulative readings at the tops of the full bars are 51, 57.5, 61, 60, and 53. Thus Navi (0.6) has the highest full-bar total, followed by Navi (0.8), while Navi (1.0) has the highest solid lower portion.
